action: Trace the gatling asset through modular and integrated ship preload selection.
observation: A modular entity with a medium autocannon selects weapon_gatling; the sampled integrated Kestrel plan selects its complete hull only. The unique Ironsong variant instead selects the generic pulse cannon.
decision: Review the gatling as a modular attachment and correct the unique-variant routing once the shared composer is free.
next: Inspect its authored material and the current renderer.
evidenceScope: Deterministic selector trace with injected equipment, not an observed gameplay encounter.
performance: The trace does not measure frame time or actual loading frequency.

action: Inspect the source image roles and the current compiled weapon payload.
observation: The authored gun has detailed panel albedo with a corresponding tangent normal and a separate material-data map. Each is 1024 square; the dated compiled package is about 3.1 MB, chiefly these three images.
decision: Retain the intentional panel detail and test lower-resolution encodings only against the live-rendered attachment.
next: Capture the packaged model and compare fit-scale quality before selecting any texture profile.
evidenceScope: Source image inspection and dated package metadata; visual renderer comparison pending.
performance: File size only; no claim about GPU memory, frame time, or frequency.

action: Inspect the packaged gatling from fitted, overhead, side and chase viewpoints.
observation: The first overhead frame drew only eight of nine target pieces and is excluded; subsequent views draw all nine. The barrel has detailed metallic machining, but the mounting rail and ammunition detail appear detached in the isolated picture.
decision: Test whether the authored detail translations were applied twice before changing the model.
next: Compare an in-memory translation correction from multiple views.
evidenceScope: Current isolated runtime renderer, not an ordinary equipped-weapon encounter.
performance: Nine target draws in complete frames; no frame-time comparison.

action: Test the three suspected doubled detail translations in the live isolated renderer.
observation: Removing the extra translations moves the previously floating feed box and rail into contact with the gun in the fitted and overhead views. All nine pieces are drawn in each before-and-after view; the prepared source retains every mesh, other transform, texture and attachment.
decision: Use the guarded source candidate as the basis for a production build after checking the mounted composition.
next: Review texture-resolution tradeoffs and the weapon when attached to a ship.
evidenceScope: Temporary matrix override in an isolated package-loader preview and an offline source-contract comparison, not an ordinary encounter.
performance: No geometry or draw-count change; no FPS measurement.

action: Compare the original, 512-pixel and 256-pixel material maps in one renderer scene.
observation: All nine target pieces draw in each comparison; at fitted, top and chase scales the 256-pixel treatment preserves the visible mechanical panel detail. The scratch render package drops from 3,122,372 to 193,100 bytes, with the original source sheets retained.
decision: Prepare a reviewed exact-hash release profile for the three existing maps, preserving the normal map and its linear encoding.
next: Check the corrected weapon on a composed ship and build the selected production package.
evidenceScope: Nine isolated package-loader views in one scene; natural equipment and closer-than-tested views remain unverified.
performance: Package byte counts only; no GPU residency or frame-time measurement.

action: Inspect the corrected compressed gatling attached to a modular craft.
observation: The candidate package loads by its content hash and mounts nine weapon pieces on the synthetic craft; baseline and candidate each show 67 target draws in close, chase and side views. At those scales the gun occupies only a small portion of the ship.
decision: Keep the placement repair and compact maps for selected release; do not claim an ordinary encounter or measured FPS improvement.
next: Publish through the selected part release and inspect the shipped package.
evidenceScope: Injected autocannon on a synthetic modular ship through the package loader; not a natural encounter.
performance: Unchanged target draw count in this preview and reduced scratch package size; no live frame-time measurement.

action: Correct the unique autocannon's modular weapon-family selection.
observation: The synthetic modular selector now resolves Ironsong through its base autocannon to the gatling; turret precedence and integrated Kestrel selection remain unchanged in focused tests.
decision: Keep the route correction while leaving natural-equipped encounter frequency unclaimed.
next: Promote the corrected gatling source and compact maps after shared build tooling is stable.
evidenceScope: Focused selector behavior and tests on synthetic entities, not an ordinary gameplay encounter.

action: Reassess the gatling texture-size study against the owner's critique.
observation: The owner rejected all shown variants: the receiver remains a flat yellow housing, with some frames washed out. The existing housing color map is uniform and its neutral normal map cannot provide physical surface detail; the compared captures also had uncontrolled environment differences.
decision: Hold promotion of the placement and compression candidate and redesign the housing surface and material response before judging the whole asset.
next: Compare generated and existing materials in one renderer scene from multiple angles and useful game scales.
evidenceScope: Owner-provided diagnostic image and source material inspection; not a natural encounter.
performance: The experiments describe encoded bytes and submissions only; no gameplay frame-time claim.

action: Generate an industrial receiver surface and compare it with the existing mechanical sheet and untextured housing in one renderer session.
observation: All nine place, top and side views drew the same nine target primitives. Both mapped sheets add some fastener and panel detail, but the housing still reads too gold and flat in the place view. Its UVs cover only a narrow portion of the texture, and its nearly uniform roughness map makes the intended ceramic surface too glossy.
decision: Reject both simple map swaps as a finished look; test UV remapping and a less glossy surface together with the corrected floating parts.
next: Inspect the remapped and matte candidates at close, top and chase scales before considering production.
evidenceScope: One synthetic package-loader session with temporary material swaps; no production change or natural encounter.
performance: Nine target draws in each trial; image residency and live frame time are not measured.

action: Diagnose why the remapped matte receiver disappeared.
observation: Removing its roughness map caused the packed-ORM shader to reference an undeclared shared texel, so the receiver did not link despite a submitted draw. A guarded stock-shader fallback now renders with each packed map absent while retaining the shared-sample path for complete maps.
decision: Keep the shared shader repair; reject the earlier missing-housing image as an invalid visual comparison.
next: Review the matte receiver after the shader fix and inspect the whole weapon's attachments.
evidenceScope: Actual package-loader renderer and focused material tests, not an ordinary encounter.
performance: No measured frame-time claim; the complete packed-map case retains its existing optimization.

action: Compare brighter generated receiver maps after correcting the shader failure.
observation: The receiver now has visible panel detail, but remains dark and warm. Top views reveal a separate long bar and block still appear detached despite the previous offset-only placement trial.
decision: Hold the complete weapon and investigate the attachment geometry; surface improvement does not make the assembly acceptable.
next: Resolve the actual bar and block interfaces and review mounted and unmounted views.
evidenceScope: Scratch texture and placement overrides on the real packaged weapon; no production promotion.
performance: Nine submitted target draws; no gameplay timing or texture-memory measurement.

action: Compare a newly generated red-oxide feed texture against sharing the receiver atlas with a red tint.
observation: Both candidates rendered in place, top and chase views. The separate generated red surface adds little discernible detail at normal size; the shared receiver atlas provides some surface variation without requiring another distinct image. Neither resolves the detached components.
decision: Keep the separate red atlas in scratch and retain the shared-atlas option for a future complete weapon candidate.
next: Finish attachment and material work before considering any package promotion.
evidenceScope: One synthetic renderer session with temporary material overrides; not a natural encounter or release asset.
performance: Nine target submissions; a shared atlas may avoid a separate texture, but GPU residency and frame time were not measured.

action: Reseat the receiver's long cantilevered rail and the separate wear plate, then compile and inspect the mounted candidate.
observation: The rail had a connected root but extended beside the barrel and looked detached; the small wear plate was outside the receiver. The scratch candidate seats a shorter underside shoe and embeds the plate without changing triangles, sockets or other materials. A later per-mesh diagnostic drew all nine gun meshes in isolated and mounted views; an earlier six-draw candidate frame remains unexplained.
decision: Keep the geometric fit as a candidate, not a finished or promoted weapon: the packaged receiver is still flat yellow.
next: Combine the corrected fit with a reviewed receiver surface and inspect the actual compiled weapon.
evidenceScope: Compiled scratch packages and game-renderer mounted/isolated diagnostics; no ordinary encounter.
performance: Nine weapon primitives and 4,432 source triangles remain unchanged; no frame-time claim.

action: Trace firing presentation and inspect the compiled mounted weapon during the existing recoil update.
observation: The sampled modular composition exposes no weaponProps/barrel binding to shipMicroMotion. At the sampled 50 and 200 ms recoil times, the gun's local matrices remain unchanged while its world transform follows hull recoil. The source muzzle and spin hooks remain present; this does not prove how every weapon type animates.
decision: Preserve simulation firing and muzzle ownership; investigate a safe weapon-specific presentation binding instead of claiming the rotary barrel already animates.
next: Determine which meshes belong to the spin hook and how fire events identify the mounted weapon before proposing motion changes.
evidenceScope: Source trace and controlled mounted renderer samples; not a natural fight.
performance: No new animation or frame-time claim.
